items.title: the function tooltip writes `: void` where the function declares NO return type - `fun f(): void` - instead of ending at the parameter list; today the signature label omits the return type exactly when the source omitted it, so a reader cannot tell a void function from one whose return type the label dropped
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): "the function tooltip to show `: void` as the return type instead of nothing when unannotated"; E9 (declaration labels for hover: `function_signature_label` / `function_signature_label_for` in analyzer.rs, `declaration_labels`); E206 (the call site's substituted second line - the same label); E299 (the `mod` line above the same fence); E278 (the hover's spelling matches an ascription's); the formatter (`vilan fmt` does NOT insert `: void` into source - the label and the source differ on purpose here)
items.body: `function_signature_label` (and the trait-member form) appends `: void` when the declaration writes no return type and the body's return type is void; a function whose return type is INFERRED non-void (a lambda-bodied `fun f() = 3`, a `fun` the analyzer typed from its tail) writes the inferred type the same way (`: i32`), so the label always carries a return type. The source is untouched (the formatter keeps `fun f() {` as written). Everywhere the label is read follows: hover, the completion detail, signature help, E206's second line, the `dbg`/explain surfaces that print a signature. Pins: a void `fun` with no annotation (`: void` shown), a `fun` with a written `: void` (unchanged), an inferred non-void, a method, a trait requirement, a closure-typed parameter's label unchanged. Sizing XS (analyzer.rs label writers + the hover/completion goldens that move).

items.title: the WRONG tooltip appears on an element head's event and chain items - hovering `on:` in `on:click(\|_\| { search_modal.open(); })` (kolt views.vl:113) and `.styled` in `.styled(const icon_button_style(style::Color::current()))` (views.vl:116) answers something other than the event hook / the `styled` method; the markup desugar's spans are answering for the written tokens
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): "the wrong tooltip appearing when hovering views.vl:113's `on:` and views.vl:116's `.styled`"; element-syntax S5 (the markup desugar: `ElementHeadItem::Event((_, name_span), _)` and `ElementHeadItem::Chain(_)` - document.rs ~1491 `collect_markup_spans`, ~1530 the suppressed `<tag` accessor, ~5222 the semantic tokens for tags and attributes); E149 (an operator token hovers as the method it dispatches to - the shape an `on:` hook's hover should take); E303 (the same head's doubled stage hints - the desugar minting two entities per item is the likely common cause); B620 (the head's method rule)
items.body: Take the repro on a kolt copy (lucide carried) at the two positions and say what each answers today (the enclosing element temporary's type? the desugared accessor? the attribute's value?). Expected: `on:` (and the event name `click`) hovers as the EVENT HOOK - the `on_click`/`on` method the desugar lowers to, fenced, with its `///` and the handler's closure type (`\|event: MouseEvent\| void`); `.styled` hovers as `styled`'s own signature on the element's type (`fun styled(self, style: Style): Button`), exactly as the same call written outside markup hovers. Cause to find: which entity `entity_at` lands on inside a head item - the desugar's synthetic call spans the whole item (name through value), so the head's written method name may be contained by, and lose to, the synthetic entity; the fix is the same span bookkeeping E303 needs (the written token's entity answers, the synthetic one is never a hover target). Pins: the two kolt positions, an attribute (`title("Search")` - hovers as the attribute), a chain item written over two lines, an event with a named handler. Sizing S (vilan-lsp document.rs `hover` + the markup span table).

items.title: an ELEMENT HEAD admits only methods that return `View` (the element itself) - a method of the element's type that returns anything else (`.len()`, `.is_some()`, a getter) is HIDDEN from completion inside an opening tag unless three characters of its name are typed (E213's rule for internal names), and, written anyway, is refused by a diagnostic that knows the method is real: "`len` is a method of `Button`, but an element head takes only methods that hand the element back (`View`); call it on a binding instead"
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): "Ban methods from the opening tag which do not return `View` if not done already (hide from auto-complete (unless 3 characters typed? I think there's a precedent for that elsewhere), but if written anyway, show a diagnostic that recognizes the method is real but simply that it shouldn't be used in here)"; the precedent is E213's internal-name rule (vilan-lsp keystroke.rs ~1229 `candidates`: an internal name is offered only to a prefix of three characters or more; document.rs's analysis completion applies the same); element-syntax S5 (`ElementHeadItem::Chain`); class-writes.md §5 (analyzer.rs ~61342: "every one of std's `View` methods hands back the element it was called on, so an element head lowers to exactly such a chain" - the invariant this item makes a RULE); A157 (a written attribute in an element head - the message shape); the element head is its own completion cursor-context (document.rs ~30370); E303 (the head's chain hints hidden - the two agree: a head's chain is View-typed by rule)
items.body: Verify first whether anything refuses it today (write `<button .len() />` and `<div .is_some()>`: expected today a type error at the CLOSE of the head, or a silent lowering, not a sentence about the head). Then two halves. (1) ANALYZER: a head's chain item must resolve to a method whose return type is the element's own type (the `View` family - `Self`/the element type, as std's attribute methods are); any other method is refused at the item's name with a diagnostic that names the method and its real owner and sends the reader to a binding ("let b = <button … />; b.len()"); a method that does not exist keeps today's member error. The lowering is unchanged for admitted methods. The rule is spelled in the spec's element-syntax section (one paragraph). Ledger rows `NEW`. (2) EDITOR: completion inside an opening tag (after `.` in a head) offers only View-returning methods of the element's type, plus attributes and `on:` hooks as today; a non-View method appears only once the typed prefix is three characters or more and matches it exactly (E213's filter, applied with the head context's own predicate - reuse `candidates`' shape, do not fork it); the hover on such a method still answers its signature (E305). Estate: kolt, the website, the examples, std's corpus - count any head item that would be refused (expected 0; say the number). Not breaking unless the estate says so (then it is a `breaking` entry with its migration). Pins: the two refused shapes, an admitted attribute method, a chain of three admitted items, completion with 0/2/3 typed characters, the hover unchanged, `vilan fmt` unchanged. Sizing S–M (analyzer.rs's element-head lowering + one diagnostic; vilan-lsp's head completion context).
